xnzbjjb.author: Plato
xnzbjjb.label: Sudden release and the ascent
xnzbjjb.translation: At first, when any of them is liberated and compelled suddenly to stand up and turn his neck round and walk and look towards the light, he will suffer sharp pains; ... And suppose once more, that he is reluctantly dragged up a steep and rugged ascent, and held fast until he's forced into the presence of the sun himself, is he not likely to be pained and irritated? When he approaches the light his eyes will be dazzled, and he will not be able to see anything at all of what are now called realities. ... And first he will see the shadows best, next the reflections of men and other objects in the water, and then the objects themselves; then he will gaze upon the light of the moon and the stars and the spangled heaven;
xnzbjjb.reading: Plato calls the release λύσις τε καὶ ἴασις, liberation and therapy, and it comes ἐξαίφνης, "suddenly": a blow of fate, a crisis or an inspiration. She reads the stages as modes of our own mind to be deconstructed, and the first seeing by starlight and moonlight as truth lived emotionally before it is understood.

s1q5ixt4.title: The ladder of virtues
steps: Political or ethical virtues: remove negative habits and purify passions such as greed, jealousy and anger
Cathartic virtues: diet, mantras, energy work, purifying the luminous body
Theoretical virtues: mathematics, the Ideas, dialectics, taught only after preparation
Paradigmatic virtues: transmissions from teacher to student through energy, symbolic objects or phrases
Theurgic virtues: rites and Mysteries that unify and bring sudden revelation
s1q5ixt4.note: Virtues are habits of being in grades; theory comes only after purification, and the summit is unification beyond words.

xon582a.author: Plato
xon582a.label: Only with those who are pregnant
xon582a.translation: And there are others, Theaetetus, who come to me apparently having nothing in them; and as I know that they have no need of my art, I coax them into marrying some one, and by the grace of God I can generally tell who is likely to do them good. ... I tell you this long story, friend Theaetetus, because I suspect, as indeed you seem to think yourself, that you are in labour--great with some conception.
xon582a.reading: Socrates does not speak with just anyone, only with those who are pregnant, and he recognises it through the ineffable. In her map of the second birth this is the stage of gestation, before the "sudden" birth into light.
